newsitem.title: HONDURAS: ACPC pow-wow kicks off deep in Honduran jungle.
newsitem.headline: ACPC pow-wow kicks off deep in Honduran jungle.

text.p: Central American members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) kicked off a regional bloc meeting here in the Honduran jungle Monday looking to analyse why world prices have spiked so sharply.

"This is going to be quick and easy," said a broadly smiling Herbert de Sola, one of El Salvador's representatives here alongside other delegates from the other regional nations Colombia, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Ecuador, as well as hosts Honduras.

Milton Mateo, spokesman for the Honduran Coffee Institute (IHCAFE), told Reuters the provisional three-point agenda was to analyse decisions taken at the fulcrum Rio de Janeiro meeting in January, where the full ACPC decided to cut export limits and further tighten supply.

Mateo said delegates would also look at updated production and export figures and also touch on the origin problems of coffee. Central America is noted for always having a certain amount of contraband coffee moving between the tiny nations.
"But we will finish today," Mateo said, stressing that there was unity in the regional camp and the meeting would not throw up any surpises for the coffee world.

Talk had been that unnamed Central American nations were seeking to loosen the ACPC's grip on exports because of the recent price bull run and that this meeting would thrash out a less rigid proposal for the full ACPC council to consider. The regional meeting has no definitive decision making capacity within the coffee cartel.

Member ACPC nations have agreed to stick to quarterly export limits in what they say is a move to control the supply of coffee but what consumer nations see is a means of tightening supplies and stocks to force up prices.
Mateo confirmed the regional meeting planned to release a statement at the end of the gathering, adding that Venezuelan representatives had been unable to attend because of flight troubles.
Copan is famous for its Mayan civilisation ruins but difficult to access as it lies close to the Guatemalan broder in a remote part of the jungle.
